SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL / FURNITURE & WORKPOINTS

Optimising office cubicle design for employee productivity and wellbeing.

Judge furniture as a working tool. This Space Craft planning note looks at optimising office cubicle design for employee productivity and wellbeing through the choices that affect everyday use, the details worth testing and the questions to take into your project brief.

Space Craft editorialPlanning note · 4 min read
IN THIS NOTEDefine the task and the userCheck the whole workpointPlan for care and changeAsk people what gets in the wayBefore you decide
01 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Define the task and the user

Consider the duration of use, range of activities and people sharing the setting. Review adjustable options and test samples rather than choosing solely from a photograph.

02 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Check the whole workpoint

The desk, chair, monitor position, power and storage function together. Test the configuration with the equipment and accessories that people actually use.

03 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Plan for care and change

Ask about warranty terms, spare parts, repair and cleaning. A furniture decision should consider the years of use ahead as well as the initial purchase.

04 / DESIGN CONSIDERATION

Ask people what gets in the way

Invite input on distractions, access, comfort and the settings people cannot currently find. A workplace brief should allow different experiences to be heard.

BEFORE YOU DECIDE

Take this into your brief.

  • Trial a representative workpoint with users.
  • Confirm dimensions, power access and cable routes.
  • Record care instructions and replacement options.

Write down one priority, one constraint and one question you still need to answer. Review them beside the plan or material sample before agreeing the next design decision.
